title: Aubrey Plaza
summary: Episode 61 opens by recapping the David Arquette night, strip-club etiquette, and Choe's invasive speculation about a private Mexico partner. Aubrey Plaza then enters to discuss a commissioned sexual painting of herself and Amy Poehler, Choe's resistance to portraiture, access and friendship, acting, Funny People, Colin Trevorrow, Nicolas Cage, and an improvised best-friend contract. The painting reveal turns into a discussion of nonconsensual penetration and a hiking rape threat; the episode then recruits Plaza into employee matchmaking and ends with wart-smelling trivia, music questions, Hollywood Game Night, and a repeated musical prayer. The editorial layer preserves the unusually revealing negotiation around creative exchange and celebrity access while rejecting coerced friendship, criminal favors, sexual-assault myths, racialized financial claims, transgender medical hearsay, third-party outing, and private contact/location publication.
sensitivity: Explicit sexual discussion; private anatomy and gender speculation; intersex and transgender slurs; sexual assault and rape threats; coercive friendship and criminal hypotheticals; opioid dependence; family finances and residence; racism and antisemitic stereotypes; employee sexual history and matchmaking; treated wart exposure; celebrity contact and home access.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 61 has 2,150 fixed-window embeddings but zero diarized turns, and no independently validated held-out multi-speaker test has passed. The explicit guest introduction supports episode structure, not publishable acoustic attribution.
